subject: Rate card and tiered-commit options for high-volume hosted API
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@edgecommerce.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@edgecommerce.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: Hosted API pricing for 15B+ tokens / month

Hi Tessa,

We’re evaluating hosted inference pricing for an upcoming expansion and expect sustained usage in the range of 12–18 billion tokens/month over the next 12 months. Can you share a baseline rate card and any tiered-commit options you offer (discounts, minimums, crediting for unused capacity, burst allowances)? Also include any SLA credit mechanics tied to latency/availability.

A few specifics that would help:
- Preferred commitment term lengths (6 / 12 / 24 months) and how discounts scale
- Do you require a minimum monthly spend to hit enterprise tiers?
- How are overages billed if we exceed committed throughput during spikes?
- Any credits or rollback protections if usage falls below commitment?

We’d also like to understand how Dedicated vs Hosted pricing differs for throughput guarantees — but for this ask, focus on hosted API economics.

I attached our short security questionnaire and a one-page usage forecast. Happy to set up a short call.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Platform Partnerships
EdgeCommerce
Attachments: EdgeCommerce_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx, usage_forecast_q4.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Hosted API pricing for 15B+ tokens / month

Hi Maya — thanks for the details and the questionnaire. Looping in Ben and Laura from Commercial to propose concrete tiers.

Quick clarifications before we build a tailored quote:
1) Is the 12–18B tokens/month an expected steady-state or a ramp that reaches ~18B at peak months?
2) What is your typical per-request latency SLO requirement (p95 target)? That informs whether we recommend a higher commit or a Dedicated pool.
3) Any data residency / VPC requirements that would affect host region?

Preliminarily, we can outline three hosted commit tiers (ballpark):
- Bronze: 0.5–2B tokens/month, small discount vs list
- Silver: 2–8B tokens/month, material discount (tiered per-2B breakpoint)
- Gold: 8B+ tokens/month, the strongest per-token discounts + optional burst buffer credits

For a 12–18B profile, customers typically consider a Gold commit for predictability; we can show blended rates and an overage rate if you'd prefer to avoid locking all capacity. Ben, Laura — can you draft two quote options (12B 12-month commit vs. 18B 12-month commit) and include SLA credit language and burst mechanics?

Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow 10:30am PT to walk through.

Best,
Tessa
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Hosted API pricing for 15B+ tokens / month — draft options

Maya — following up with concrete draft options based on the numbers you shared. I’ve kept these as hosted-API focused offers; we can also provide a Dedicated proposal if you want hard throughput SLOs.

Summary (all $/1K tokens):
- Option A — 12B commit / 12 months (blended): $7.50 per 1K tokens
  - Overage: $10.00 per 1K tokens (billed monthly)
  - Burst buffer: 15% of committed throughput for short spikes (no extra charge if under buffer)
  - Unused commit: credit rollover up to 2 months; after that credits expire

- Option B — 18B commit / 12 months (blended): $6.25 per 1K tokens
  - Overage: $8.50 per 1K tokens
  - Burst buffer: 25% of committed throughput for short spikes
  - Unused commit: credit rollover up to 3 months; option for quarterly true-ups

Other commercial mechanics
- Minimum monthly spend to qualify for Gold pricing: $40K/month effective (before overages)
- SLA credit: availability <99.5% or p95 latency > configured SLO triggers a service credit up to 10% of monthly bill depending on severity and duration (detailed schedule in formal SLA)
- Early termination: pro-rated repayment of initial commit credits beyond 60 days unless we agree a wind-down schedule

Notes:
- We can add a “ramp discount” for the first 2 months if you expect a significant ramp from lower usage.
- For long-term commitments (24 months) we can shave another ~5–7% off per-token pricing and increase the burst buffer.

I attached a short one-page summary (initial_ratecard_summary.pdf). If this looks in the ballpark, I’ll push a formal quote and draft contract language to DocuSign.

Thanks — Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: initial_ratecard_summary.pdf

From: Maya Singh <maya@edgecommerce.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeCommerce Procurement <procurement@edgecommerce.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Hosted API pricing for 15B+ tokens / month — draft options

Ben/Tessa — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups: 
- Our finance team prefers the 18B / 12-month structure if we can get the blended $6.25/1K and the 25% burst buffer. Please confirm whether that price is conditional on a $40K/mo minimum spend, or if the blended price is guaranteed once the 18B commit is signed.
- We’d like the unused commit credit to be bankable for at least 3 months; quarterly true-ups are fine.
- For overage protection, can you confirm whether overages during a sustained spike (longer than 48 hours) are billed at overage rates or treated as billable burst and throttled? We need clarity for budgeting.

Can you produce a formal quote (DocuSign) with the following attachments included: your ratecard summary, the SLA schedule, and our completed security questionnaire (attached). We’ll circulate to procurement and legal.
